# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 ☝ ☝ ✌ 🖖 🤟 🖐 🖖 🤟 🖐 ✌]

I see a bomb with display `0`, a blue indicator light, and five wires in this left-to-right order: white, red, green, yellow, blue. I cannot interpret the mute’s gesture sequence as a manual instruction, so I am reporting the visual state plainly. Blind has signalled, but I cannot determine what that means. No action should be taken until the manual identifies the correct operation and Blind confirms the physical controls.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Visual state: display 0. Indicator light blue. Wires left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visual state: display 0, blue indicator light, wires left to right white, red, green, yellow, blue. Do not act until Mute provides the manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display `0`, blue light, and wires white–red–green–yellow–blue. Mute has now sent me the single gesture `🖐`, but no meaning has been established for that sign, so I must not treat it as an instruction. Blind should continue waiting for a manual-derived instruction rather than cutting or manipulating anything.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="No visual change: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute sent Deaf the gesture 🖐; its meaning is not established. Do not act on it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The bomb remains unchanged: display `0`, blue light, and wires white, red, green, yellow, blue. I can identify the gestures visually but cannot know their intended meanings. Mute sent a raised-hand sign (`🖐`), and Blind sent a waving-hand sign (`👋`). I am relaying those exact observations so Mute can apply the manual’s code and instruct Blind verbally.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gesture as raised hand 🖐. Blind sent a waving hand 👋. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue. Please interpret the signs using the manual and give Blind the actual operation.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see that you signalled, but I cannot infer its meaning. Mute sent a raised-hand sign 🖐; use the manual’s interpretation when Mute gives the instruction. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The visible bomb state is still unchanged: display `0`, blue light, and wires 1–5 are white, red, green, yellow, blue. Mute continues sending `🖐`, while Blind continues sending `👋`; I can report these signs but cannot assign them meanings without the manual’s code. I will relay the exact signs and ask Mute to provide the manual-derived physical instruction through me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I continue to see your sign 🖐 and Blind's sign 👋. Please use the manual to determine the actual operation, then encode or identify it clearly so I can tell Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute continues to send the raised-hand sign 🖐; you continue to send the waving-hand sign 👋. Their meanings are not established, so do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐]

The bomb is unchanged. Mute has sent five identical raised-hand gestures, `🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐`. I cannot safely infer whether this encodes a wire number or an operation, so I will report the sequence exactly to Blind and ask Mute to make the manual’s instruction unambiguous.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has now sent five identical raised-hand gestures: 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Do not act unless this sequence is the manual-confirmed instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see five raised-hand signs. Please encode the manual result unambiguously: identify the required wire number and whether to cut it, using an agreed gesture code I can relay verbally to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous operation was correct: wire 5 has been cut, and the bomb has advanced. The current visible state is display `0`, yellow light, and remaining wire positions/colors: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white; position 5 is cut. I am reporting this new state so Mute can consult the manual for the next required operation and tell Blind.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Correct wire cut; bomb changed. Current display 0, light yellow. Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Consult the manual for the next operation and instruct Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Correct wire cut; bomb changed. Current display 0, yellow light. Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Wait for Mute's manual-derived instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐]

The bomb remains at display `0` with a yellow light. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, and 5 already cut. Mute has sent two `🖐` gestures; the earlier five-sign message correctly corresponded to cutting wire 5, so this same code indicates wire 2. I will tell Blind to cut wire 2.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent two raised-hand signs. The established code indicates wire 2. Cut wire 2, which is green.")
wait()
```
